title: Hard input probability as a preimage measure
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, and let $S$ be a set of pairs $(A,B)$ of subsets of $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$. Then the real-valued probability that the pair of input sets $(X,Y)$ generated by the hard input distribution lies in $S$ equals the real-valued measure, under the hard-distribution measure on the sample space, of the preimage $\{\omega : (X(\omega),Y(\omega)) \in S\}$ — that is, the probability assigned to $S$ by the hard input distribution is computed by pulling $S$ back through the input map to the explicit hard sample space.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a set of pairs of subsets of $\{0,\dots,n-1\}$
